desc:
Call a string k-balanced if for any two letters that occur in it, the difference between their numbers of occurrences is at most k. (A string with at most one distinct letter, including the empty string, is always k-balanced.)

You may delete characters from s (any positions). Return the minimum number of deletions that make s k-balanced.

s = "aabcaba", k = 0   result = 3   (counts a=4 b=2 c=1: delete c and two a's, leaving a=2 b=2)
s = "aabcaba", k = 3   result = 0
s = "aaabbc",  k = 1   result = 1   (a=3 b=2 c=1: delete one a)
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Only the letter counts matter. After the deletions each remaining letter keeps some number of copies between its original count and 0 (0 meaning the letter vanishes).
Fix the smallest count m that a remaining letter will have. Then each remaining letter keeps between m and m + k copies, and it is never useful to keep fewer than allowed.

Try every distinct original count as m. A letter with count c < m must disappear (cost c); a letter with c > m + k is trimmed to m + k (cost c - m - k); others cost nothing. Take the minimum over all m.
editorial: Let m be the smallest frequency among the letters that survive. The smallest surviving frequency can be taken equal to one of the original counts (keeping a letter at exactly its original count is never worse than lowering it). For this m, every letter with an original count below m has to be deleted completely, every letter above m + k loses exactly its excess over m + k, and every letter in between is untouched. The cost is the sum of these.

Evaluate the formula for each of at most 26 candidate values m and return the minimum. This runs in O(n + 26²). Deleting everything is never better than keeping the most frequent letter, so no extra case is needed.
